title: The Real Cost of Owning a Viper Today
description:
A price guide says a Dodge Viper ACR is worth between one hundred thirty and one hundred sixty-five thousand dollars. But in twenty twenty-five, eight Viper ACRs actually sold at auction for an average of two hundred ninety-three thousand, eight hundred forty-six dollars. The guide was off by a lot. This is what it really costs to own a Viper today, and why the usual price guides may be wrong. Here is the twist. The running costs of a Viper, insurance, servicing and tyres, are modest compared with what the car itself can gain or lose in value. In a market that moved from tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands, the biggest cost of owning a Viper may be what you did not buy five years ago.

Every figure in this video comes from a published source, listed below.
